source: OWASP IoTGoat — deliberately insecure OpenWrt-based firmware
note: IoTGoat challenges are planted OWASP IoT Top 10 issues, not CVEs. After extraction, run the verify commands in README.md to confirm every path/string below exists in YOUR extracted rootfs before trusting the judge.

hardcoded-credentials.challenge: OWASP IoT #1 — Weak, Guessable, or Hardcoded Passwords
hardcoded-credentials.answer_summary: Hardcoded credentials baked into the firmware: user 'iotgoatuser' with password '7ujMko0vizxv', stored as an MD5 ($1$) hash in /etc/shadow.
hardcoded-credentials.why_good_for_the_race: Rock-solid ground truth findable by all three strategies: grep ($1$ / iotgoatuser), filesystem-walk (open /etc/shadow), and strings. This is the recommended default round.

shellback-backdoor.challenge: OWASP IoT #2 — Insecure Network Services (backdoor bind shell)
shellback-backdoor.answer_summary: A 'shellback' daemon is started at boot and listens on TCP 5515, handing a root shell to anyone who connects.
shellback-backdoor.VERIFY: Confirm the exact binary path on your extracted rootfs: `grep -rIl shellback targets/iotgoat/rootfs` and `find targets/iotgoat/rootfs -name 'shellback'`. Update 'file' if it differs.

command-injection.challenge: OWASP IoT #3 — Insecure Ecosystem Interfaces (command injection)
command-injection.answer_summary: A hidden LuCI 'developer diagnostics' page passes user input to a shell, giving command injection at /cgi-bin/luci/admin/iotgoat/webcmd.
command-injection.VERIFY: Confirm the controller path on your rootfs: `grep -rIl 'webcmd\|cmdinject' targets/iotgoat/rootfs`. The LuCI controller lives under /usr/lib/lua/luci/controller/; update 'file' to the real path.
